items.question: What can you throw in C# versus JavaScript?
items.answer: C# throw requires a System.Exception (or derived type). JavaScript throw accepts any value — strings, numbers, plain objects — which makes catch typing guesswork. On the Common Language Runtime (CLR) the thrown object carries Message, StackTrace, InnerException, and sometimes HResult. Uncaught exceptions kill the thread; in a hosted process they can take down the application.

items.sixtySeconds: Throw Exception types only. JS can throw anything. Unobserved tasks are module 13.

items.question: When do you catch in a queue worker versus letting it bubble?
items.answer: Catch at the message boundary when you can log, retry with backoff, or send to a dead-letter queue (DLQ) and complete the receive. Catching Exception and swallowing leaves poison messages looping or causes silent data loss. Framework and host-level handlers exist for unhandled exceptions; bubbling is correct when you cannot restore state. Use when filters to catch transient faults without hiding bugs.
followUps: Where does finally run relative to a rethrow?
items.sixtySeconds: Worker boundary: recover, retry, DLQ. Unknown failures bubble. Do not empty-catch Exception.

items.question: throw versus throw ex versus wrapping?
items.answer: throw; rethrows the current exception and keeps the original StackTrace. throw ex; starts a new throw site and you lose the original frames — the classic bug. Wrapping is new OuterException(message, inner) when the caller needs a domain-level type plus the root cause. Never wrap just to log; log and throw; or wrap once at a boundary.
followUps: Why is catch (Exception) { throw; } sometimes still wrong?
items.sixtySeconds: throw; keeps the stack. throw ex; destroys it. Wrap with InnerException at boundaries.

items.question: How do you dispose a SkiaSharp SKSurface correctly?
items.answer: SKSurface, SKCanvas, SKBitmap, and SKPaint hold native resources. Implement or consume IDisposable and wrap with using (or await using for async equivalents). The compiler emits try/finally so Dispose runs on exceptions and returns. Do not wait for a finalizer — that is module 14 and too late for native memory under high-concurrency image work.
items.sixtySeconds: using owns IDisposable. SkiaSharp is native. Finalizers later. await using for async disposal.

items.question: Explain try, catch, finally, and when filters.
items.answer: try marks risky work. catch handles a compatible exception type — most derived first. finally always runs for that try, even on rethrow. when adds a filter: catch (HttpRequestException ex) when (ex.StatusCode == TooManyRequests) handles throttling without catching other HTTP failures. Filters should be fast and side-effect free.
followUps: Does finally run before return inside try?
What is a bare catch without a type?
items.sixtySeconds: try/catch/finally plus when filters. finally always runs. Most-derived catch first.

items.question: When should you use Result<T> instead of throwing exceptions?
items.answer: Use Result or Try-methods for expected failures — validation, not-found, bad CSV rows — where failure is normal and hot. Reserve exceptions for invariant breaks, unrecoverable I/O, and programmer bugs. Exceptions allocate and walk the stack; Result keeps control flow explicit at service boundaries.
followUps: Does the BCL use Result everywhere?
How do you still log root cause when returning Result?
items.sixtySeconds: Result for expected outcomes. Exceptions for exceptional. TryParse pattern in BCL. Catch at worker boundary with when for transient HTTP.

items.question: What happens if Dispose throws inside finally?
items.answer: If Dispose throws during finally while another exception is unwinding, the original exception can be lost unless you capture both. Prefer using statements and implement Dispose without throwing. In custom types, catch inside Dispose only to avoid masking, log, and optionally rethrow.
followUps: What is the Dispose pattern versus a finalizer?
items.sixtySeconds: using emits try/finally plus Dispose. Dispose throw during unwind hides original. SkiaSharp needs deterministic Dispose. Finalizers module 14.

items.question: How do exception filters (when) differ from catching inside the handler?
items.answer: when is evaluated after the type matches but before the catch body runs. It lets you catch HttpRequestException only for 429 without catching other HTTP errors. Keep filters fast and side-effect free — no logging or I/O inside when.
followUps: Can when access local variables from the try block?
items.sixtySeconds: when filters after type match. Use for transient status codes. No side effects in filter. Most-derived catch still first.
